category: PSpice waveform viewer (Probe) window operations, display control, data exchange and application settings
description: Menu commands and dialogs of the PSpice A/D application window as documented in the PSpice 17.4 help: trace management, Plot menu (axis settings, extra Y axes and plots, labels, digital size), View zoom and window modes, Display Control and plot window templates, clipboard/data export and import, the Probe Settings dialog, large-data handling, printing, Tools menu extras (Generate Report, FRA, PSpice Calculator, MATLAB), keyboard shortcuts, pspice.ini Probe keys and documented limits.

tools.name: Trace > Delete All Traces / Undelete Traces
tools.description: Delete All Traces clears every trace from the selected plot; Undelete Traces restores the traces removed last. Individual traces are deleted by selecting their legend names (Shift-click for several) and pressing Delete or Cut.
tools.usage: Trace > Delete All Traces (Ctrl+Delete)  |  Trace > Undelete Traces (Ctrl+U)
tools.example: Ctrl+Delete to clear the plot, Insert to add new traces, Ctrl+U if you removed the wrong ones.

tools.name: Trace Properties (right-click trace > Properties)
tools.description: Sets colour, line pattern, width and legend symbol of one or several selected traces, with an option to draw the symbol on the trace itself. Double-clicking a legend name instead opens Modify Trace to edit the expression.
tools.usage: Select trace(s) (Shift+click or Edit > Select All) > right-click > Properties

parameters.name: Color / Pattern / Width
parameters.description: Line appearance, also used by Print Preview and printouts.

parameters.name: Symbol / Show Symbol
parameters.description: Legend marker and whether it appears on the trace.

tools.example: Edit > Select All, right-click > Properties > Width = thickest, to prepare plots for a report.
tools.notes: Assigned colours stay when traces are deleted; applying a new colour scheme in Tools > Options reassigns them. Use View > Redraw if changes do not appear.

tools.name: Trace Information (Section Information dialog)
tools.description: Shows the trace name, the data file it came from when several .dat files are loaded, the simulation that produced it (for example the parametric value or Monte Carlo run of the section) and the number of data points. It is the quickest way to identify which curve of a family belongs to which run.
tools.usage: Right-click a trace > Information, or double-click the trace symbol in the legend
tools.example: After a .STEP of Rload, right-click the outlying curve > Information to read Rload for that section.

tools.name: Plot > Axis Settings
tools.description: Tabbed dialog defining the X axis (data range, linear/log scale, Use Data full or restricted, processing option Fourier or Performance Analysis, axis title and axis variable), the Y axes (range, scale, axis number, position, title) and the X/Y grids (automatic or major/minor spacing). Save as Default stores the settings for new axes; Reset Defaults restores factory values.
tools.usage: Plot > Axis Settings..., or double-click the axis area

parameters.name: Use Data: Restricted
parameters.description: Limits the data used by measurements, AVG/RMS and FFT to a range.

parameters.name: Processing Options
parameters.description: Fourier or Performance Analysis mode for the plot.

parameters.name: Axis Variable
parameters.description: Any trace expression can become the X axis (e.g. V(in) for a transfer curve).

tools.example: X Axis tab: Use Data = Restricted 9m to 10m, then evaluate RMS(I(C1)) or Swing_XRange over exactly the last cycles.
tools.notes: FFT results are only clean over an integral number of periods, so restricting the data is the standard way to prepare a Fourier plot.

tools.name: Log X Axis / Log Y Axis (toolbar toggles)
tools.description: Probe toolbar buttons that switch the X or Y axis of the selected plot between linear and logarithmic scaling, equivalent to the Linear/Log option in Plot > Axis Settings.
tools.usage: Probe toolbar: Log X axis / Log Y axis buttons
tools.example: Plot impedance magnitude M(V(a)/I(Vtest)) and toggle Log Y to see decades of impedance.
tools.notes: Log scaling of a Y axis fails for traces that contain zero or negative values.

tools.name: Plot > Add Y Axis / Delete Y Axis
tools.description: Adds another Y axis to the selected plot (up to three); the new axis becomes the selected axis and subsequent traces are drawn on it. Delete Y Axis removes the selected axis together with its traces.
tools.usage: Plot > Add Y Axis (Ctrl+Y)  |  Plot > Delete Y Axis (Shift+Ctrl+Y)
tools.example: Add VDB(out), then Ctrl+Y and add VP(out) to get magnitude and phase on one Bode plot.

tools.name: Plot > Add Plot to Window / Delete Plot
tools.description: Adds a new, empty plot above the selected plot in the same Probe window, sharing the X axis, or deletes the selected plot. Multiple stacked plots keep voltages, currents and digital signals readable on a common time base.
tools.usage: Plot > Add Plot to Window  |  Plot > Delete Plot
tools.example: Plot > Add Plot to Window, click the new plot, then Trace > Add Trace I(L1) so inductor current sits above the output voltage.

tools.name: Plot > Unsynchronize X Axis
tools.description: Gives the selected plot its own X axis so it can use different scaling, Fourier mode or Performance Analysis independently of the other plots in the window. Plots from the same data are otherwise synchronised.
tools.usage: Select a plot > Plot > Unsynchronize X Axis
tools.example: Top plot: V(out) versus time; add a plot, unsynchronize it and switch it to Fourier to see the spectrum at the same time.
tools.notes: Unsynchronising cannot be undone; delete the plot and add a new one to resynchronise.

tools.name: Plot > Digital Size
tools.description: Sets the fraction of the plot used by the digital trace area and the width reserved for digital trace names. The same can be done by dragging the separator between the analog and digital areas.
tools.usage: Plot > Digital Size...

parameters.name: Percentage of Plot to be Digital
parameters.description: Height share of the digital area.

parameters.name: Length of Digital Trace Name
parameters.description: Characters reserved for names.

tools.example: Plot > Digital Size > 60 % when a mixed-signal plot holds many digital buses.

tools.name: Plot > Label (Text, Line, Poly-line, Arrow, Box, Circle, Ellipse, Mark)
tools.description: Annotation objects placed on analog plots: text up to 124 characters, lines, poly-lines, arrows, boxes, circles, ellipses with an inclination angle, and Mark, which pins the most recently moved cursor's coordinates to the trace. Labels are moved by dragging and edited with Edit > Modify Object.
tools.usage: Plot > Label > Text | Line | Poly-line | Arrow | Box | Circle | Ellipse | Mark
tools.example: Move cursor 1 to the overshoot peak (Cursor Max) then Plot > Label > Mark to annotate the value.
tools.notes: Probe rescales the plot to keep all labels visible unless the axis range is user-defined.

tools.name: Plot > AC / DC / Transient (analysis selection)
tools.description: When a data file holds results of more than one analysis type, these checked items select which analysis the active plot displays. Opening such a file also prompts with the Analysis Type and Available Sections dialogs.
tools.usage: Plot > AC  |  Plot > DC  |  Plot > Transient
tools.example: A profile with bias point, DC sweep and transient: switch the plot to DC to view the transfer curve, then Window > New Window for the transient.

tools.name: View > Zoom (Fit, In, Out, Area, Previous, Redraw, Pan - New Center)
tools.description: Zoom commands for the Probe plot: Fit shows all data and labels, In/Out zoom by a factor of 2 around a picked point, Area zooms to a dragged box, Previous restores the prior view, Redraw refreshes, and Pan - New Center recentres at the same scale.
tools.usage: View > Zoom > Fit | In (Ctrl+I) | Out (Ctrl+T) | Area (Ctrl+A) | Previous | Redraw (Ctrl+L) | Pan - New Center
tools.example: Ctrl+A and drag around a switching edge, then View > Zoom > Previous to return.

tools.name: PSpice keyboard shortcuts (Probe window)
tools.description: Default keys of the PSpice waveform window: Insert adds traces, Ctrl+Delete deletes all traces, Ctrl+U restores deleted traces, Ctrl+Y / Shift+Ctrl+Y add or delete a Y axis, F12 restores the last Probe window session, and Shift+Ctrl with a letter drives the cursor (C display, F freeze, S search, X max, M min, P peak, T trough, L slope, I point, N/R next/previous transition). Arrow, Home/End keys move cursor 1; with Shift they move cursor 2; with Ctrl they jump between traces.
tools.usage: Insert | Ctrl+Delete | Ctrl+U | Ctrl+Y | F12 | Shift+Ctrl+C/F/S/X/M/P/T/L/I/N/R | arrows, Home, End
tools.example: Shift+Ctrl+C to show cursors, Shift+Ctrl+X to jump cursor 1 to the maximum, Shift+Right arrow to step cursor 2.
tools.notes: Keyboard shortcuts can be customised from Tools > Customize.

tools.name: Window > Display Control
tools.description: Saves the complete configuration of a Probe window (plots, traces, labels, axis settings and X variable) as a named display in a .prb file and restores it later, even for a new simulation as long as the variable names match. Displays can be copied or deleted and loaded from other .prb files.
tools.usage: Window > Display Control > Displays tab: New Name + Save | Save To | Restore | Load | Copy To | Delete | Delete From

parameters.name: Save / Save To
parameters.description: Store in the current local .prb or another file.

parameters.name: Restore
parameters.description: Recreate the saved window.

tools.example: Set up V(out), I(L1) and a Fourier plot, Display Control > New Name 'converter_view' > Save; after the next run choose it and click Restore.

tools.name: Plot window templates (Display Control > Templates tab)
tools.description: Reusable displays whose node voltages, pin currents or power names are replaced by arguments, so the same plot layout (for example a Bode plot or rise-time plot) can be applied to any design. Templates are saved in local, global or other .prb files and restored by assigning real nodes to each argument, or placed in Capture as square template markers.
tools.usage: Window > Display Control > Templates tab (Save/Save To, Restore, Properties, Load, Copy To, Delete); Capture: PSpice > Markers > Plot Window Templates

parameters.name: Argument Type
parameters.description: any, current, power or voltage.

parameters.name: Store Template In
parameters.description: Local File, Global File or Other File.

tools.example: In Capture, PSpice > Markers > Plot Window Templates > pick a Bode template > Place, then click the input and output nets; the next run opens the template filled in.
tools.notes: Only templates matching the active analysis type are listed; some predefined ones need multi-run analyses. Loaded templates are not saved with the data file.

tools.name: Window > Copy to Clipboard
tools.description: Copies the active Probe window as a bitmap to the Windows clipboard for pasting into reports, optionally with transparent window and plot backgrounds and a chosen foreground colour. Menu and status bars are not included.
tools.usage: Window > Copy to Clipboard (dialog: transparent backgrounds, foreground colour options)
tools.example: Window > Copy to Clipboard > Make window and plot backgrounds transparent > OK, then paste into Word.

tools.name: Copy trace data (Edit > Copy on selected traces)
tools.description: Copies the X and Y data points of the selected traces as tab-delimited text, ready to paste into Excel, MATLAB or a text file. It is the quickest way to post-process a few traces outside PSpice.
tools.usage: Click trace name(s) in the legend (Shift/Ctrl+click for more) > Edit > Copy (Ctrl+C) > paste in the target application
tools.example: Select V(out) and I(L1) legend names, Ctrl+C, paste into Excel and chart or compute custom metrics.
tools.notes: For many variables or large runs use File > Export > Text instead.

tools.name: File > Export (Probe Data .dat, Stimulus library .stl, Text .txt)
tools.description: Writes selected output variables to a new waveform data file, to a stimulus library (so a simulated waveform can drive another circuit) or to a text file. Filters list analog, digital, voltage, current, power, noise, alias and subcircuit variables; transient exports can be compressed with absolute and relative tolerances.
tools.usage: File > Export > Probe Data (.dat) | Stimulus library (.stl) | Text (.txt)

parameters.name: Output Variables to Export
parameters.description: Variables moved over with Add / Add All.

parameters.name: Data Compression
parameters.description: Transient only: Enable, Absolute and Relative Tolerances to thin the points.

tools.example: File > Export > Stimulus library > add V(sensor_out) > sensor.stl, then use it as a PWL stimulus in the next stage's design.

tools.name: File > Import (traces from .txt or .csv)
tools.description: Imports tabular waveform data, such as a digital oscilloscope capture, from a text or CSV file into a new .dat file so it can be overlaid on simulation results. You choose which column is the X axis and name it Time, Frequency or a sweep variable.
tools.usage: File > Import > choose .txt/.csv > Import Traces dialog (DAT File Path, X-Axis, Available/Imported Traces)

parameters.name: X-Axis
parameters.description: Column used as X; renamed Time, Frequency or a user sweep variable.

parameters.name: Add / Add All / Remove
parameters.description: Choose which columns become traces.

tools.example: Import scope.csv with X-Axis = Time, then add V(out)@f1 and the imported trace @f2 in one plot for correlation.

tools.name: File > Open (waveform data file)
tools.description: Opens a .dat file in a new Probe window. If the file contains several analysis types the Analysis Type dialog asks which one to show, and for multi-run data the Available Sections dialog lets you pick sections (or All); simulation errors stored in the file are offered for viewing.
tools.usage: File > Open (Ctrl+O) > select .dat > Analysis Type / Available Sections dialogs
tools.example: Open a Monte Carlo .dat and select only sections 1 (nominal) and 17 (the failing run) to compare them.
tools.notes: File > Close closes all data files of the selected plot window and any other windows using them.

tools.name: Tools > Options (Probe Settings: General tab)
tools.description: Global Probe window preferences: use of trace symbols, trace colour scheme (Normal, Match Axis, Sequential Per Axis, Unique By File), scroll bars, auto-update interval during simulation, number of histogram divisions for Monte Carlo Performance Analysis, number of cursor digits, and check boxes for Mark Data Points, Display Evaluation, Display Statistics and Highlight Error States.
tools.usage: Tools > Options > General tab

parameters.name: Number of Histogram Divisions
parameters.description: Bins for Performance Analysis histograms.

parameters.name: Auto-Update Interval
parameters.description: Auto, every N seconds or every N percent of the run.

parameters.name: Mark Data Points
parameters.description: Draws each simulated point, revealing coarse time steps.

tools.example: Tools > Options > Mark Data Points to check whether the max step size is small enough around an edge.
tools.notes: Per-profile Probe behaviour (when Probe opens, which markers to show) is set in the simulation profile's Probe Window tab instead.

tools.name: Probe Settings: Large Data tab and View > Large Data File Mode
tools.description: Controls how data files with more points per trace than a threshold (default 1,000,000) are loaded: display a complete but decimated trace using fewer points, display accurate trace parts one at a time, always ask, or ignore the warning. In parts mode, View > Load Next Part (or the toolbar button) steps through the file.
tools.usage: Tools > Options > Large Data tab; View > Large Data File Mode > Display fewer points | Display in parts; View > Load Next Part

parameters.name: Data points in one part
parameters.description: Threshold and part size (default 1000000).

parameters.name: Always ask / Ignore this Warning
parameters.description: Whether the Large Data File dialog appears.

tools.example: A 20 ms switching simulation with 5 M points: choose Display in parts to measure edges accurately, Display fewer points for an overview.
tools.notes: Decimated traces are not accurate enough for measurements; both reduced modes are disabled for marching waveforms. Ignoring the warning can end in an Out of Memory error.

tools.name: Probe Settings: Cursor Settings, Color Settings and Font Settings tabs
tools.description: Remaining Probe Settings tabs: Cursor Settings sets the number of cursor digits (2-18) and can bring back the old non-dockable cursor window; Color Settings selects the application theme (Dark or Light) and colour schemes; Font Settings sets plot fonts.
tools.usage: Tools > Options > Cursor Settings | Color Settings | Font Settings

parameters.name: Application Theme
parameters.description: Dark or Light (standard Windows dialogs do not follow it).

tools.example: Tools > Options > Color Settings > Application Theme = Light before capturing plots for a printed report.

tools.name: View > Alternate Display / Always on Top
tools.description: Alternate Display toggles between the standard layout (Probe window, output window and simulation status window with all toolbars) and a minimal layout with only the plots, each remembering its own toolbar settings. Always on Top (push-pin button) keeps the PSpice window above Capture so waveforms can be watched while cross-probing the schematic.
tools.usage: View > Alternate Display (toolbar button); View > Always on Top (push pin)
tools.example: Switch to Alternate Display, pin it on top, shrink it beside the Capture page and click nets to cross-probe.

tools.name: View > Output File / Circuit File / Simulation Messages
tools.description: Open the text outputs of the current simulation inside PSpice: the .out file (echoed netlist, bias point, tables, warnings), the circuit file (.cir) actually simulated, and the simulation message list with errors and warnings. Selecting a message in the Simulation Status window and pressing F1 opens help for it.
tools.usage: View > Output File | Circuit File | Simulation Messages
tools.example: After a convergence failure, View > Output File and search for 'ERROR' or the last reported time point.
tools.notes: Edit > Toggle Line Number Display, Goto Line and Find (with regular expressions) work in these text views.

tools.name: PSpice window panes (Output, Simulation Status, Cursor and Command windows)
tools.description: View menu toggles for the dockable panes of the PSpice application: Output Window (messages), Simulation Status Window (progress, analysis, time step, errors), Cursor Window, Command Window, Status Bar and Workbook Mode (tabbed windows).
tools.usage: View > Output Window | Simulation Status Window | Cursor Window | Command Window | Status Bar | Workbook Mode
tools.example: View > Simulation Status Window during a long transient to watch the time step shrink before a convergence problem.

tools.name: View > Simulation Queue (batch simulation)
tools.description: Lists pending simulations and their order when several .sim or .cir files are opened together. Files can be added from other folders, reordered, reset, their profiles edited through Settings, and the batch started.
tools.usage: File > Open Simulation > multi-select .sim/.cir files (Ctrl/Shift) > Open > Simulation Queue dialog: Add | up/down | Reset | Settings | Start; View > Simulation Queue to monitor
tools.example: Open tran.sim, ac.sim and mc.sim together, order them in the Simulation Queue and press Start before leaving for the night.
tools.notes: For fully unattended runs from scripts use pspice -r or psp_cmd.exe instead.

tools.name: Simulation menu (Run, Pause, Stop, Save, Edit Profile, Edit Runtime Settings)
tools.description: Controls of the simulator inside PSpice: run the current simulation, pause or stop it, save it, open the Simulation Settings of the profile, and edit settings that can be changed while a simulation is paused.
tools.usage: Simulation > Run <name> | Pause | Stop | Save | Edit Profile | Edit Runtime Settings
tools.example: Pause a long transient, inspect waveforms, adjust runtime settings, then Run to continue.

tools.name: Tools > Customize (PSpice toolbars and commands)
tools.description: Shows or hides toolbars, drags commands from any menu category onto toolbars or menus, removes buttons and resets toolbars. Toolbar arrangements are saved per display mode.
tools.usage: Tools > Customize > Toolbars tab (show, Reset, Reset All) | Commands tab (drag buttons)
tools.example: Tools > Customize > Commands > Trace category > drag 'Evaluate Measurement' next to Add Trace.

tools.name: File > Page Setup (plots per page, header and footer codes)
tools.description: Sets print margins, 1-9 plots per page, orientation, border and plot title, where cursor information is printed, and header/footer text. Header and footer fields accept codes that insert date, time, page number and simulation information from the data file.
tools.usage: File > Page Setup > Header... / Footer... with codes &D &T &N &A &M &I &E &P

parameters.name: &D / &T / &N
parameters.description: Current date, current time, page number.

parameters.name: &A / &M
parameters.description: Simulation date and time from the data file.

parameters.name: &I / &E / &P
parameters.description: Simulation title, temperature, and the parameter changing between sections.

tools.example: Footer centre: '&I  T=&E  &P', right: 'page &N', then File > Print Preview.
tools.notes: Printed line width is scaled automatically; PRINTERLINEWIDTH in the [Probe] section of pspice.ini overrides it.

tools.name: File > Print / Print Preview / Printer Setup
tools.description: Prints selected plots of the current Probe window, each on its own page unless Page Setup combines them, with a choice of automatic grid spacing based on the print area or the screen. Print Preview shows the pages first and Printer Setup selects printer, paper and orientation.
tools.usage: File > Print (Ctrl+P) | Print Preview | Printer Setup

parameters.name: Plots to Print
parameters.description: Which plots of the window to print.

parameters.name: Automatic Grid Spacing
parameters.description: Based on Print Area or Same as Display.

tools.example: File > Print > select plots 1 and 2 > Same as Display > OK.

tools.name: pspice.ini [PROBE] section keys
tools.description: Probe settings stored in pspice.ini, most of which mirror the Probe Settings dialog but some are only editable in the file: PRBFILE names the global .prb file, CURSORNDIGITS, HISTNDIVISIONS, HISTSHOWSTATSON, MARKDATAPOINTS, DISPLAYEVALON, AUTOUPDATEINTERVAL with AUTOUPDATEPERCENT/AUTOUPDATESECONDS, DGTLNAMELEFTJUSTIFY and PRINTERLINEWIDTH.
tools.usage:
[PROBE]
PRBFILE=<global.prb>
CURSORNDIGITS=5
HISTNDIVISIONS=10
MARKDATAPOINTS=ON|OFF

parameters.name: PRBFILE
parameters.description: Global .prb loaded whenever a data file is opened.

parameters.name: AUTOUPDATEINTERVAL
parameters.description: Auto, Seconds or Percent (default AUTO).

parameters.name: HISTNDIVISIONS
parameters.description: Histogram divisions (default 10).

tools.example:
[PROBE]
PRBFILE=C:\team\probe\team_measurements.prb
HISTNDIVISIONS=20
tools.notes: Close all PSpice applications before editing; keyword=value with no spaces around '='; comment lines start with ';'. pspice.ini normally lives next to pspice.exe in <install>\tools\pspice.

tools.name: pspice.ini [Probe Display Colors] section
tools.description: Screen colour definitions for the waveform window: background, foreground and trace 1 to trace 12, given as colour names or R G B values 0-255, plus numtrace colors to set how many colours are used before repeating. A [Probe Printer Colors] section does the same for printing.
tools.usage:
[Probe Display Colors]
background=<color>
foreground=<color>
trace_1=<color> ... trace_12=<color>

parameters.name: color names
parameters.description: black blue green cyan red magenta yellow brightwhite brown lightgray darkgray darkblue darkgreen darkcyan darkred darkmagenta, or 'R G B'.

tools.example:
[Probe Display Colors]
background=brightwhite
foreground=black
trace_1=0 0 255
tools.notes: Takes effect the next time PSpice starts. The Dark/Light theme in Tools > Options covers most needs without editing the file.

tools.name: Tools > Generate Report (HTML transient report)
tools.description: Creates an HTML report from transient analysis data containing general information (data file, analysis, circuit, simulation time, PSpice version), lists of nets and devices, and current, voltage and power data. The report template is the Tcl script orPspReport.tcl and can be customised.
tools.usage: Tools > Generate Report (template: <install>\tools\pspice\tclscripts\orPspReport.tcl)
tools.example: After a transient run, Tools > Generate Report and attach the HTML to a design review.
tools.notes: Requires transient data of analog devices; the HTML file is limited to 800 MB.

tools.name: Tools > FRA (Frequency Response Analysis)
tools.description: Enables Frequency Response Analysis, which injects signals into a circuit during transient simulation and extracts gain and phase with Fourier analysis, giving Bode plots of circuits such as switching converters that have no valid small-signal AC model.
tools.usage: Tools > FRA
tools.example: Open the shipped example under <install>\tools\pspice\capture_samples\anasim\fra, run it and inspect the extracted loop gain.
tools.notes: The FRA example also demonstrates the MINSIMPTS option and the .PROBE64 command used for accurate data. FRA runs are much slower than .AC because each frequency needs settled transient cycles.

tools.name: Tools > PSpice Calculator > Hysteresis Core Loss
tools.description: Built-in calculator in the PSpice application that estimates hysteresis core loss for magnetic components, complementing the CORE model and the Magnetic Parts Editor when sizing inductors and transformers.
tools.usage: Tools > PSpice Calculator > Hysteresis Core Loss
tools.example: Run a transient of a flyback, then Tools > PSpice Calculator > Hysteresis Core Loss for the transformer core.

tools.name: Tools > Matlab (Set Matlab Path, Start Engine, Export Traces, Co-Simulation)
tools.description: MATLAB integration from the PSpice window: set the MATLAB installation path, start the MATLAB engine, export all or only selected traces into the MATLAB workspace for post-processing, and launch MATLAB for PSpice-Simulink co-simulation.
tools.usage: Tools > Matlab > Set Matlab Path | Start Engine | Export All Traces | Export Selected Traces | Co-Simulation
tools.example: Tools > Matlab > Set Matlab Path, Start Engine, select V(out) and I(L1) > Export Selected Traces, then analyse them with MATLAB's fft().
tools.notes: Requires a compatible MATLAB release; co-simulation additionally needs the PSpice Systems Option (SLPS).

tools.name: File > Change Product
tools.description: Changes the product license PSpice runs under, when more than one PSpice product license is available on the license server. It is the in-application counterpart of the product choice offered when PSpice starts.
tools.usage: File > Change Product
tools.example: File > Change Product > pick the higher-tier PSpice product listed, then reopen the simulation that needs its features.
tools.notes: Only products that are actually licensed are offered; the exact product names depend on the release (OrCAD 17.4 vs OrCAD X) and your license file.

tools.name: PSpice text editor functions (Edit menu for .cir, .out and .lib files)
tools.description: PSpice includes a text editor for circuit, output, library and include files with undo/redo, find and replace (match case, regular expressions, wrap around, Mark All), Goto Line, Insert File, line-number display and bookmarks. File > New > Text File creates a new file.
tools.usage: Edit > Find (Ctrl+F) | Find Next (F3) | Replace (Ctrl+H) | Goto Line (Ctrl+G) | Insert File | Toggle Line Number Display | Toggle/Next/Previous/Clear Bookmarks

parameters.name: Regular expression
parameters.description: Supports . [ ] ^ $ * + ? | and backslash escapes.

tools.example: View > Output File, Edit > Find with regular expression '^ERROR' and Mark All.
tools.notes: Undo/Redo apply to the text editor only, not to Probe actions.

tools.name: Limits in PSpice and Probe
tools.description: Documented capacity limits: up to 400 analog traces and 400 digital traces per display, or twice the number of sections if greater; about 2^31 analog nodes and 2^15 digital nodes per .dat file; and 10,000 runs for a PSpice Monte Carlo analysis.
tools.usage: Reference values (PSpice help, Reference Information > Limits in PSpice and Probe)
tools.example: A 20,000-run Monte Carlo must be split into two .MC runs with different seeds.
tools.notes: Advanced Analysis Monte Carlo has its own limit of 5,000 runs.

tools.name: Invalid node name characters (PSpice)
tools.description: Characters that must not be used in net or wire names for PSpice because they are reserved or unrecognised: @ % & * ? ~ # ^ " \ ! ( ) ' < > = [ ] and spaces, plus + as an initial character. The word CN is also reserved for canonical names.
tools.usage: Reference list (PSpice help, Invalid node names)
tools.example: Rename a net 'VOUT+' to 'VOUT_P' and 'CLK#' to 'CLK_N' before simulating.
tools.notes: Capture translates some pin-name characters in PSPICETEMPLATE (< to l, > to g, = to e), but net names are passed as written.
